finding.claim: The purge handler calls checkPerm(u, "admin") but discards the boolean result, so the admin check is never enforced. Any caller who reaches the handler can run purgeAll().
finding.source: Any authenticated (non-admin) user sending a request to the purge endpoint; the user comes from the request context via userFrom(r)
finding.sink: purgeAll() at handlers.go:27, a destructive admin-only operation

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) gets the requesting user, with no admin requirement
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for a non-admin, but the result is ignored

finding.guards_checked: The sibling rotateKeys handler correctly uses mustPerm and returns on failure, but purge does not. I found no middleware or other guard in the repo (handlers.go is the only file). Checked the case where checkPerm's result is used; it is not used here.

verdict.guard_found: none (checkPerm at handlers.go:12-14 returns a bool that is discarded at line 26; no middleware or other files exist)
verdict.reason: handlers.go:26 calls checkPerm(u, "admin"), which only returns a bool (handlers.go:12-14), and discards the result, so purgeAll() at handlers.go:27 runs for any user, unlike rotateKeys, which tests mustPerm at handlers.go:33.
